headline: 🔥 225 WILLOW POINT HAS TAKEN THREE TOURS IN TWENTY-ONE HOURS AFTER TAKING NONE IN ITS FIRST THREE DAYS — 9:00 AM and noon today, from two different brokerages, plus yesterday's 4:30. ⚠️ ZERO FEEDBACK FORMS HAVE COME BACK ON ANY OF THE THREE, and this address has never once sent a REQUESTED notice — only CONFIRMED — so the scheduler is not going to tell you how they went. ⭐ CALL BOTH OF TODAY'S AGENTS THIS AFTERNOON: a market that finds a house all at once is telling you something about the price, and the two people who can say what it is walked through it a few hours ago.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THREE TOURS IN TWENTY-ONE HOURS ON A FOUR-DAY-OLD LISTING THAT HAD NEVER BEEN SHOWN. Lindsey H. of Epique walked it 9:00–9:30 this morning; Anna C. of A Squared Properties walked it 12:00–12:30, booked only four hours ahead; a third agent booked 4:00 PM and cancelled ten minutes later. Two different brokerages inside one morning, on top of yesterday's first-ever 4:30.
hotSignals.action: Call Lindsey H. and Anna C. this afternoon, before the day gets away — no feedback form exists on this address and none is coming, because it has never sent a REQUESTED notice in its life. Ask each the same two questions: how did it show against what else they are seeing, and is the number right. Then call the Stricklands with both answers — the seller update draft in your Gmail was written when there was one showing and is now two behind.

hotSignals.signal: ⚖️ THE COUNTER IS LIVE AND THE PAPER IS THEIRS TO SEND. Your seller approved the $443,000 counter at 9:01 this morning — “we are good to go with your recommendation” — you answered at 9:17, and it went to the buyer's agent at 10:00 with the furniture carve-out, acknowledged at 10:01. The buyer's last number was $434,000.
hotSignals.action: Chase the paperwork, not the price: the written counter coming back and the preapproval, which is now about a day late. And keep saying the real risk out loud to your seller — these buyers must close their own house first, which makes this a contingency rather than a closing.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 STILL THE BEST BUYER READ ON THE BOARD AND NOW ON DAY SEVEN. Amy G. of Ethos International filed interested — YES and wrote that her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and it is at the TOP of their list. She also phoned from inside the house mid-showing, so this is a returned call, not a cold one. She left “priced right” blank and reported the basement lights would not come on.
hotSignals.action: Call her — do not write. Two questions: what would it take, and what is behind the blank price answer. Then answer the basement lights, which is the only complaint on this file nobody has addressed and is probably a breaker, not a repair bill.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 NOT A SHOWINGTIME FORM — THE BUYER HIMSELF, BY TEXT. Adin D. named his gap under the ask, told you to save his number as a standing investor buyer, and wrote “Happy to have you represent me.” A fourth independent agent read landed Thursday calling the price too high, with staging scored 1 of 5 and a pre-inspection named as the cheaper fix.
hotSignals.action: Call Adin, then take the four-read stack to the institutional seller — the ask is not a debate anymore, and the agent handed you a lever that is not a price cut.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE STRONGEST SINGLE WORD ANY AGENT HAS FILED ON THIS BOARD, AND IT IS NOW THIRTEEN DAYS OLD. Wanda W. of Millennium Homes answered the interest question with “Very” — not yes, very — on a weekend when two other agents in the same 24 hours filed not interested.
hotSignals.action: Call her. Thirteen days of silence on a “very” is the cheapest loss on this whole board, and she is the only one of the three who wanted it.
